sanskrit: vaidyāś cāpy āturāḥ santi balavantaḥ sudurbalāḥ strīmantaś ca tathā ṣaṇḍhā vicitraḥ kālaparyayaḥ
english: Even physicians fall ill; the strong become utterly weak; men rich in women turn impotent—strange is the turning of time.

sanskrit: kule janma tathā vīryam ārogyaṃ dhairyam eva ca saubhāgyam upabhogaś ca bhavitavyena labhyate
english: Birth in a noble house, valor, health, and steadfastness, good fortune and enjoyment—all are won only through what is destined to be.

sanskrit: santi putrāḥ subahavo daridrāṇām anicchatām bahūnām icchatāṃ nāsti samṛddhānāṃ viceṣṭatām
english: The poor, who wish for none, have sons in abundance; while the wealthy, striving and longing for many, have none at all.

sanskrit: vyādhir agnir jalaṃ śastraṃ bubhukṣā śvāpadaṃ viṣam rajjvā ca maraṇaṃ jantor uccācca patanaṃ tathā
english: Disease, fire, water, the sword, starvation, beasts of prey, poison, death by the noose, and a fall from a height—such are a creature's ends.

sanskrit: niryāṇaṃ yasya yad diṣṭaṃ tena gacchati hetunā dṛśyate nābhyatikrāmann atikrānto na vā punaḥ
english: Whatever departure is appointed for a man, by that cause he goes; none is seen to overpass it, nor, once it is past, to be subject to it again.

sanskrit: dṛśyate hi yuvaiveha vinaśyan vasumān naraḥ daridraś ca parikliṣṭaḥ śatavarṣo janādhipa
english: For here, O lord of men, a wealthy man is seen to perish while still young, and a poor man, sorely afflicted, lives a hundred years.

sanskrit: akiṃcanāś ca dṛśyante puruṣāś cirajīvinaḥ samṛddhe ca kule jātā vinaśyanti pataṃgavat
english: Men who possess nothing are seen to live long, while those born in a prosperous house perish like moths in a flame.

sanskrit: prāyeṇa śrīmatāṃ loke bhoktuṃ śaktir na vidyate kāṣṭhāny api hi jīryante daridrāṇāṃ narādhipa
english: In this world the prosperous, for the most part, have no power to enjoy; yet the poor, O ruler of men, can digest even wood.

sanskrit: aham etat karomīti manyate kālacoditaḥ yad yad iṣṭam asaṃtoṣād durātmā pāpam ācaran
english: "It is I who do this," thinks the man driven by time—the evil-souled one, committing every kind of sin out of his discontent and craving.

sanskrit: striyo 'kṣā mṛgayā pānaṃ prasaṅgān ninditā budhaiḥ dṛśyante cāpi bahavaḥ saṃprasaktā bahuśrutāḥ
english: Women, dice, the hunt, and drink—these attachments the wise condemn; yet many men, even the deeply learned, are seen ensnared by them.

sanskrit: iti kālena sarvārthānīpsitānīpsitāni ca spṛśanti sarvabhūtāni nimittaṃ nopalabhyate
english: Thus, through time, all things—desired and undesired alike—come to touch every being, and no cause for it can be found.

sanskrit: vāyum ākāśam agniṃ ca candrādityāv ahaḥkṣape jyotīṃṣi saritaḥ śailān kaḥ karoti bibharti vā
english: The wind, the ether, and fire, the moon and the sun, day and night, the stars, the rivers, and the mountains—who makes or sustains them?

sanskrit: śītam uṣṇaṃ tathā varṣaṃ kālena parivartate evam eva manuṣyāṇāṃ sukhaduḥkhe nararṣabha
english: Cold and heat, and the rains as well, revolve in their turn by time; even so, O bull among men, do the joys and sorrows of mortals.

sanskrit: nauṣadhāni na śāstrāṇi na homā na punar japāḥ trāyante mṛtyunopetaṃ jarayā vāpi mānavam
english: Neither herbs nor scriptures, neither oblations nor recitations can save a man once he is overtaken by death or by old age.

sanskrit: yathā kāṣṭhaṃ ca kāṣṭhaṃ ca sameyātāṃ mahodadhau sametya ca vyatīyātāṃ tadvad bhūtasamāgamaḥ
english: As two logs of driftwood come together upon the great ocean, and having met, drift apart again—such is the meeting of beings.

sanskrit: ye cāpi puruṣaiḥ strībhir gītavādyair upasthitāḥ ye cānāthāḥ parānnādāḥ kālas teṣu samakriyaḥ
english: Those attended by retinues of men and women, by song and music, and those who are forlorn, living on others' food—toward all of these time acts alike.

sanskrit: mātṛpitṛsahasrāṇi putradāraśatāni ca saṃsāreṣv anubhūtāni kasya te kasya vā vayam
english: Thousands of mothers and fathers, and hundreds of sons and wives, have been experienced through our wanderings in existence—whose are they, and whose are we?

sanskrit: naivāsya kaś cid bhavitā nāyaṃ bhavati kasya cit pathi saṃgatam evedaṃ dārabandhusuhṛdgaṇaiḥ
english: No one truly belongs to him, nor does he belong to anyone; this gathering with wife, kin, and the host of friends is but a meeting upon the road.

sanskrit: kvāsaṃ kvāsmi gamiṣyāmi ko nv ahaṃ kim ihāsthitaḥ kasmāt kam anuśoceyam ity evaṃ sthāpayen manaḥ anitye priyasaṃvāse saṃsāre cakravad gatau
english: "Where was I? Where am I? Where shall I go? Who indeed am I, and to what end do I abide here? Wherefore, and for whom, should I grieve?"—thus should one steady the mind, when union with what is dear is impermanent and the round of existence turns like a wheel.

sanskrit: na dṛṣṭapūrvaṃ pratyakṣaṃ paralokaṃ vidur budhāḥ āgamāṃs tv anatikramya śraddhātavyaṃ bubhūṣatā
english: The wise know that the world beyond is never seen beforehand by direct perception; yet one who wishes to prosper must place his faith without transgressing the sacred traditions.

sanskrit: kurvīta pitṛdaivatyaṃ dharmāṇi ca samācaret yajec ca vidvān vidhivat trivargaṃ cāpy anuvrajet
english: One should perform the rites due to the ancestors and the gods, and practice the duties of dharma; the learned man should offer sacrifice according to the ordinance, and pursue the threefold aim of dharma, artha, and kāma.

sanskrit: saṃnimajjaj jagad idaṃ gambhīre kālasāgare jarāmṛtyumahāgrāhe na kaś cid avabudhyate
english: This whole world is sinking down into the deep ocean of time, where old age and death are the great sea-monsters—and not one being is aware of it.

sanskrit: āyurvedam adhīyānāḥ kevalaṃ saparigraham dṛśyante bahavo vaidyā vyādhibhiḥ samabhiplutāḥ
english: Many physicians, who have studied the whole science of medicine together with its appurtenances, are seen overwhelmed by diseases.

sanskrit: te pibantaḥ kaṣāyāṃś ca sarpīṃṣi vividhāni ca na mṛtyum ativartante velām iva mahodadhiḥ
english: Though they drink astringent decoctions and clarified butters of many kinds, they cannot pass beyond death, any more than the great ocean passes beyond its shore.

sanskrit: rasāyanavidaś caiva suprayuktarasāyanāḥ dṛśyante jarayā bhagnā nagā nāgair ivottamaiḥ
english: Even those skilled in elixirs, who have administered their tonics well, are seen broken by old age, as trees are broken by mighty elephants.

sanskrit: tathaiva tapasopetāḥ svādhyāyābhyasane ratāḥ dātāro yajñaśīlāś ca na taranti jarāntakau
english: Likewise, those rich in austerity, devoted to the study of scripture, the givers of gifts and the performers of sacrifice—none of these cross beyond old age and death.

sanskrit: na hy ahāni nivartante na māsā na punaḥ samāḥ jātānāṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ na pakṣā na punaḥ kṣapāḥ
english: For the days never return, nor the months, nor again the years; for all beings that are born, neither the fortnights return nor the nights.

sanskrit: so 'yaṃ vipulam adhvānaṃ kālena dhruvam adhruvaḥ naro 'vaśaḥ samabhyeti sarvabhūtaniṣevitam
english: Helplessly, in the course of time, this perishable man sets out upon that vast and certain road which is traveled by all beings.

sanskrit: deho vā jīvato 'bhyeti jīvo vābhyeti dehataḥ pathi saṃgatam evedaṃ dārair anyaiś ca bandhubhiḥ
english: Either the body departs from the living soul, or the soul departs from the body; this companionship with wife and other kinsmen is but a meeting upon the road.

sanskrit: nāyam atyantasaṃvāso labhyate jātu kena cit api svena śarīreṇa kim utānyena kena cit
english: No everlasting union is ever obtained by anyone, not even with one's own body—how much less, then, with any other?

sanskrit: kva nu te 'dya pitā rājan kva nu te 'dya pitāmahaḥ na tvaṃ paśyasi tān adya na tvāṃ paśyanti te 'pi ca
english: Where now, O king, is your father today? Where now is your grandfather? You do not see them now, nor do they see you.

sanskrit: na hy eva puruṣo draṣṭā svargasya narakasya vā āgamas tu satāṃ cakṣur nṛpate tam ihācara
english: For no man is a witness of heaven or of hell; but the sacred tradition is the eye of the good—O king, follow it here.

sanskrit: caritabrahmacaryo hi prajāyeta yajeta ca pitṛdevamaharṣīṇām ānṛṇyāyānasūyakaḥ
english: Having fulfilled the vow of chastity, one should beget offspring and offer sacrifice, free of envy, that he may discharge his debt to the ancestors, the gods, and the great seers.

sanskrit: sa yajñaśīlaḥ prajane niviṣṭaḥ; prāg brahmacārī pravibhaktapakṣaḥ ārādhayan svargam imaṃ ca lokaṃ; paraṃ ca muktvā hṛdayavyalīkam
english: Devoted to sacrifice and settled in the begetting of offspring, having first lived as a chaste student and apportioned his obligations, he wins both heaven and this world, having cast away the falsehood that lay within his heart.

sanskrit: samyag ghi dharmaṃ carato nṛpasya; dravyāṇi cāpy āharato yathāvat pravṛttacakrasya yaśo 'bhivardhate; sarveṣu lokeṣu carācareṣu
english: For a king who duly practices dharma and gathers wealth as is fitting, whose wheel of sovereignty rolls onward, his fame grows ever greater throughout all worlds, moving and unmoving.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca ity evam ājñāya videharājo; vākyaṃ samagraṃ paripūrṇahetuḥ aśmānam āmantrya viśuddhabuddhir; yayau gṛhaṃ svaṃ prati śāntaśokaḥ
english: Vyāsa said: Having thus understood this discourse in its fullness, complete in its reasoning, the king of Videha, his understanding purified, took leave of Aśman and went home, his grief stilled.

sanskrit: tathā tvam apy acyuta muñca śokam; uttiṣṭha śakropama harṣam ehi kṣātreṇa dharmeṇa mahī jitā te; tāṃ bhuṅkṣva kuntīsuta mā viṣādīḥ
english: So too do you, O unfaltering one, let go of grief; arise, you who are the equal of Śakra, and come to gladness. By the dharma of the warrior the earth has been won by you; enjoy it, O son of Kuntī, and do not despair.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca avyāharati kaunteye dharmaputre yudhiṣṭhire guḍākeśo hṛṣīkeśam abhyabhāṣata pāṇḍavaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: While Yudhiṣṭhira, the son of Kuntī and son of Dharma, kept silent, Guḍākeśa the Pāṇḍava addressed Hṛṣīkeśa.

sanskrit: jñātiśokābhisaṃtapto dharmarājaḥ paraṃtapaḥ eṣa śokārṇave magnas tam āśvāsaya mādhava
english: "Tormented by grief for his kinsmen, the Dharma King, scorcher of foes, is here sunk in an ocean of sorrow—console him, O Mādhava.

sanskrit: sarve sma te saṃśayitāḥ punar eva janārdana asya śokaṃ mahābāho praṇāśayitum arhasi
english: We are all once more cast into doubt, O Janārdana; you, O mighty-armed one, are able to dispel his sorrow."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu govindo vijayena mahātmanā paryavartata rājānaṃ puṇḍarīkekṣaṇo 'cyutaḥ
english: Thus addressed by the great-souled Vijaya, Govinda the lotus-eyed, the unfaltering one, turned toward the king.

sanskrit: anatikramaṇīyo hi dharmarājasya keśavaḥ bālyāt prabhṛti govindaḥ prītyā cābhyadhiko 'rjunāt
english: For Keśava was one whom the Dharma King could not refuse; from boyhood onward Govinda had been dearer to him even than Arjuna.

sanskrit: saṃpragṛhya mahābāhur bhujaṃ candanabhūṣitam śailastambhopamaṃ śaurir uvācābhivinodayan
english: Taking hold of the king's arm, anointed with sandal and like a pillar of stone, the mighty-armed scion of Śūra spoke, seeking to comfort him.

sanskrit: śuśubhe vadanaṃ tasya sudaṃṣṭraṃ cārulocanam vyākośam iva vispaṣṭaṃ padmaṃ sūryavibodhitam
english: Resplendent was Kṛṣṇa's face, with its fair teeth and lovely eyes, like a full-blown, unfolded lotus awakened by the sun.

sanskrit: mā kṛthāḥ puruṣavyāghra śokaṃ tvaṃ gātraśoṣaṇam na hi te sulabhā bhūyo ye hatāsmin raṇājire
english: "Do not grieve, O tiger among men, with the grief that wastes the body; for those who fell on this field of battle are not to be easily regained.

sanskrit: svapnalabdhā yathā lābhā vitathāḥ pratibodhane evaṃ te kṣatriyā rājan ye vyatītā mahāraṇe
english: As gains obtained in a dream prove false upon waking, even so, O king, are those warriors who have passed away in the great battle.

sanskrit: sarve hy abhimukhāḥ śūrā vigatā raṇaśobhinaḥ naiṣāṃ kaś cit pṛṣṭhato vā palāyan vāpi pātitaḥ
english: For all those heroes, the ornaments of war, departed facing the foe; not one of them was struck down from behind, nor while fleeing.

sanskrit: sarve tyaktvātmanaḥ prāṇān yuddhvā vīrā mahāhave śastrapūtā divaṃ prāptā na tāñ śocitum arhasi
english: All those heroes, having yielded up their own lives fighting in the great combat, purified by the sword, have attained heaven; you ought not to grieve for them.

sanskrit: atraivodāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam sṛñjayaṃ putraśokārtaṃ yathāyaṃ prāha nāradaḥ
english: On this very matter they recite an ancient tale—how Nārada spoke to Sṛñjaya, who was stricken with grief for his son.

sanskrit: sukhaduḥkhair ahaṃ tvaṃ ca prajāḥ sarvāś ca sṛñjaya avimuktaṃ cariṣyāmas tatra kā paridevanā
english: "I and you, O Sṛñjaya, and all creatures alike, shall move on, never released from joys and sorrows—what, then, is there to lament?

sanskrit: mahābhāgyaṃ paraṃ rājñāṃ kīrtyamānaṃ mayā śṛṇu gacchāvadhānaṃ nṛpate tato duḥkhaṃ prahāsyasi
english: Hear of the supreme good fortune of kings, as I recount it; give heed, O monarch, and thereafter you will cast off your sorrow.

sanskrit: mṛtān mahānubhāvāṃs tvaṃ śrutvaiva tu mahīpatīn śrutvāpanaya saṃtāpaṃ śṛṇu vistaraśaś ca me
english: Hearing of those mighty kings who have died, drive away your anguish; listen to me in full detail.

sanskrit: āvikṣitaṃ maruttaṃ me mṛtaṃ sṛñjaya śuśruhi yasya sendrāḥ savaruṇā bṛhaspatipurogamāḥ devā viśvasṛjo rājño yajñam īyur mahātmanaḥ
english: Hear from me, O Sṛñjaya, that Marutta, son of Avikṣit, has died—he to whose sacrifice the gods came, the all-creating ones, with Indra and Varuṇa, led by Bṛhaspati, to that great-souled king.

sanskrit: yaḥ spardhām anayac chakraṃ devarājaṃ śatakratum śakrapriyaiṣī yaṃ vidvān pratyācaṣṭa bṛhaspatiḥ saṃvarto yājayām āsa yaṃ pīḍārthaṃ bṛhaspateḥ
english: He who drew Śakra, the king of the gods, lord of a hundred sacrifices, into rivalry; whom the learned Bṛhaspati, wishing to please Śakra, refused to officiate for—and for whom Saṃvarta then conducted the rites, to vex Bṛhaspati.

sanskrit: yasmin praśāsati satāṃ nṛpatau nṛpasattama akṛṣṭapacyā pṛthivī vibabhau caityamālinī
english: While that king, best of monarchs, ruled the good, the earth shone forth, ripening her crops untilled, and garlanded with sacred shrines.

sanskrit: āvikṣitasya vai satre viśve devāḥ sabhāsadaḥ marutaḥ pariveṣṭāraḥ sādhyāś cāsan mahātmanaḥ
english: At the great sacrifice of Avikṣit's son, the All-Gods were the assembly-members, the Maruts were the servers, and the Sādhyas too attended that great-souled king.

sanskrit: marudgaṇā maruttasya yat somam apibanta te devān manuṣyān gandharvān atyaricyanta dakṣiṇāḥ
english: When the hosts of the Maruts drank Marutta's soma, the sacrificial gifts he gave surpassed those given to gods, to men, and to Gandharvas alike.

sanskrit: sa cen mamāra sṛñjaya caturbhadrataras tvayā putrāt puṇyataraś caiva mā putram anutapyathāḥ
english: If even he died, O Sṛñjaya—he who was richer than you in the four blessings and more meritorious than your son—then do not grieve for your son.

sanskrit: suhotraṃ ced vaitithinaṃ mṛtaṃ sṛñjaya śuśruma yasmai hiraṇyaṃ vavṛṣe magahvān parivatsaram
english: We have heard, O Sṛñjaya, that Suhotra, son of Vitithi, has died—he for whom Maghavān rained down gold for a whole year.

sanskrit: satyanāmā vasumatī yaṃ prāpyāsīj janādhipa hiraṇyam avahan nadyas tasmiñ janapadeśvare
english: He upon whose accession the earth, called "the wealth-bearing," became true to her name, O lord of men; while that ruler of the realm reigned, the rivers carried gold.

sanskrit: kūrmān karkaṭakān nakrān makarāñ śiṃśukān api nadīṣv apātayad rājan maghavā lokapūjitaḥ
english: Maghavān, honored by the world, O king, let fall into the rivers tortoises and crabs, crocodiles and sea-monsters and dolphins—all of gold.

sanskrit: hairaṇyān patitān dṛṣṭvā matsyān makarakacchapān sahasraśo 'tha śataśas tato 'smayata vaitithiḥ
english: Seeing the golden fish, sea-monsters, and turtles fallen by the thousands and hundreds, the son of Vitithi then smiled.

sanskrit: tad dhiraṇyam aparyantam āvṛttaṃ kurujāṅgale ījāno vitate yajñe brāhmaṇebhyaḥ samāhitaḥ
english: That boundless gold, gathered together in the Kurujāṅgala, he distributed with a collected mind to the brāhmaṇas as he sacrificed at the outspread rite.

sanskrit: sa cen mamāra sṛñjaya caturbhadrataras tvayā putrāt puṇyataraś caiva mā putram anutapyathāḥ adakṣiṇam ayajvānaṃ śvaitya saṃśāmya mā śucaḥ
english: If even he died, O Sṛñjaya—he who was richer than you in the four blessings and more meritorious than your son—then do not grieve for your son, who gave no sacrificial gifts and offered no sacrifice; be calm, O son of Śvitya, and do not mourn.

sanskrit: aṅgaṃ bṛhadrathaṃ caiva mṛtaṃ śuśruma sṛñjaya yaḥ sahasraṃ sahasrāṇāṃ śvetān aśvān avāsṛjat
english: We have heard, O Sṛñjaya, that Aṅga, of the great chariot, has died—he who set free a thousand thousand white horses.

sanskrit: sahasraṃ ca sahasrāṇāṃ kanyā hemavibhūṣitāḥ ījāno vitate yajñe dakṣiṇām atyakālayat
english: And a thousand thousand maidens, adorned with gold, he drove forth as sacrificial fee while sacrificing at the outspread rite.

sanskrit: śataṃ śatasahasrāṇāṃ vṛṣāṇāṃ hemamālinām gavāṃ sahasrānucaraṃ dakṣiṇām atyakālayat
english: A hundred hundred-thousands of bulls, garlanded with gold, each followed by a thousand cows, he drove forth as the sacrificial fee.

sanskrit: aṅgasya yajamānasya tadā viṣṇupade girau amādyad indraḥ somena dakṣiṇābhir dvijātayaḥ
english: While Aṅga sacrificed upon the mountain at Viṣṇu's stride, Indra grew exhilarated with the soma, and the twice-born with the sacrificial gifts.

sanskrit: yasya yajñeṣu rājendra śatasaṃkhyeṣu vai punaḥ devān manuṣyān gandharvān atyaricyanta dakṣiṇāḥ
english: At his sacrifices, O lord of kings, numbering a hundred over and over, the gifts he gave surpassed those given to gods, to men, and to Gandharvas.

sanskrit: na jāto janitā cānyaḥ pumān yas tat pradāsyati yad aṅgaḥ pradadau vittaṃ somasaṃsthāsu saptasu
english: No man has been born, nor will another be born, who shall bestow such gifts as the wealth Aṅga gave away at the seven forms of the soma sacrifice.

sanskrit: sa cen mamāra sṛñjaya caturbhadrataras tvayā putrāt puṇyataraś caiva mā putram anutapyathāḥ
english: If even he died, O Sṛñjaya—he who was richer than you in the four blessings and more meritorious than your son—then do not grieve for your son.

sanskrit: śibim auśīnaraṃ caiva mṛtaṃ śuśruma sṛñjaya ya imāṃ pṛthivīṃ kṛtsnāṃ carmavat samaveṣṭayat
english: We have heard, O Sṛñjaya, that Śibi, son of Uśīnara, has died—he who could roll up this whole earth like a hide.

sanskrit: mahatā rathaghoṣeṇa pṛthivīm anunādayan ekacchatrāṃ mahīṃ cakre jaitreṇaikarathena yaḥ
english: Making the earth resound with the great roar of his chariot, he brought the world under a single parasol with his one victorious car.

sanskrit: yāvad adya gavāśvaṃ syād āraṇyaiḥ paśubhiḥ saha tāvatīḥ pradadau gāḥ sa śibir auśīnaro 'dhvare
english: As many cattle and horses as there are today, together with the beasts of the wild—so many cows did Śibi, son of Uśīnara, bestow at his sacrifice.

sanskrit: nodyantāraṃ dhuraṃ tasya kaṃ cin mene prajāpatiḥ na bhūtaṃ na bhaviṣyantaṃ sarvarājasu bhārata anyatrauśīnarāc chaibyād rājarṣer indravikramāt
english: Prajāpati deemed that none could bear his burden—none past nor yet to come among all kings, O Bhārata—save Śaibya, son of Uśīnara, the royal seer of Indra's prowess.

sanskrit: sa cen mamāra sṛñjaya caturbhadrataras tvayā putrāt puṇyataraś caiva mā putram anutapyathāḥ adakṣiṇam ayajvānaṃ taṃ vai saṃśāmya mā śucaḥ
english: If even he died, O Sṛñjaya—he who was richer than you in the four blessings and more meritorious than your son—then do not grieve for your son, who gave no sacrificial gifts and offered no sacrifice; be calm and do not mourn.

sanskrit: bharataṃ caiva dauḥṣantiṃ mṛtaṃ sṛñjaya śuśruma śākuntaliṃ maheṣvāsaṃ bhūridraviṇatejasam
english: We have heard, O Sṛñjaya, that Bharata, son of Duḥṣanta, has died—the son of Śakuntalā, the great archer of abundant wealth and splendor.

sanskrit: yo baddhvā triṃśato hy aśvān devebhyo yamunām anu sarasvatīṃ viṃśatiṃ ca gaṅgām anu caturdaśa
english: He who bound thirty horses for the gods along the Yamunā, twenty along the Sarasvatī, and fourteen along the Gaṅgā.

sanskrit: aśvamedhasahasreṇa rājasūyaśatena ca iṣṭavān sa mahātejā dauḥṣantir bharataḥ purā
english: With a thousand horse-sacrifices and a hundred rājasūyas did Bharata, son of Duḥṣanta, of great splendor, perform his rites of old.

sanskrit: bharatasya mahat karma sarvarājasu pārthivāḥ khaṃ martyā iva bāhubhyāṃ nānugantum aśaknuvan
english: The mighty deeds of Bharata, among all kings, the other princes could not attain, even as mortals cannot reach the sky with their arms.
